jp-20260920-news-1.title: Respect for the Aged Day: Census Bureau Statistics Show Elderly Population Reaches Record High, Working Seniors Also at Peak Levels

segments.src: ## 65歳以上人口、過去最多を更新
segments.tr: ## Population Aged 65 and Over Reaches Record High

segments.src: 「敬老の日」にあわせて総務省が公表した人口推計によると、日本の65歳以上人口は過去最多を更新したとみられる。総人口に占める65歳以上の割合(高齢化率)も過去最高の水準に達しており、世界的に見ても類を見ない速さで高齢化が進んでいる状況があらためて浮き彫りになった。
segments.tr: According to population estimates released by the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications on the occasion of Respect for the Aged Day, Japan's population aged 65 and over appears to have reached a record high. The proportion of those aged 65 and over in the total population (aging rate) has also reached its highest level ever, and it has become increasingly clear that Japan is aging at an unprecedented pace globally.

segments.src: 総務省はこの時期、住民基本台帳などをもとにした人口推計を毎年公表しており、少子化による総人口の減少と、高齢者数の増加が同時に進んでいることが特徴となっている。年代別に見ても、75歳以上のいわゆる後期高齢者の割合が高まっている傾向がうかがえる。
segments.tr: Each year at this time, the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications releases population estimates based on the basic resident registry and other sources. A key characteristic is that the total population is decreasing due to the declining birthrate while the number of elderly people is increasing simultaneously. Looking at age groups, there is a clear trend of an increasing proportion of those aged 75 and over, the so-called oldest-old population.

segments.src: ## 働く高齢者の数も最高水準に
segments.tr: ## Number of Working Seniors Also at Peak Levels

segments.src: 今回の発表であわせて注目されたのが、就業している高齢者数の推移だ。総務省の労働力調査などのデータでは、65歳以上で働く人の数がここ数年増加を続けており、過去最多の水準に達したとみられる。就業者全体に占める高齢者の比率も上昇傾向にある。
segments.tr: What also drew attention in this announcement was the trend in the number of employed elderly people. According to data from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' Labor Force Survey and other sources, the number of people working at age 65 and over has continued to increase in recent years and appears to have reached a record high. The proportion of elderly workers in the total employed population is also on an upward trend.

segments.src: 背景には、健康寿命の延伸により働く意欲・体力のある高齢者が増えていることに加え、多くの業種で人手不足が深刻化していることがある。企業側にとっても、経験豊富な人材を確保できるメリットは大きく、定年延長や再雇用制度を整備する動きが広がっている。
segments.tr: Behind this trend is the growing number of elderly people with the motivation and physical capacity to work, thanks to increases in healthy life expectancy, as well as severe labor shortages in many industries. For companies as well, the benefits of securing experienced talent are substantial, and efforts to extend retirement ages and implement re-employment systems are spreading.

segments.src: ## 人手不足と年金財政、二つの視点
segments.tr: ## Two Perspectives: Labor Shortages and Pension Finance

segments.src: 高齢者の就業拡大は、人手不足に悩む現場にとっては歓迎される一方、制度面ではいくつかの論点も指摘されている。
segments.tr: While expanded employment of the elderly is welcomed by workplaces struggling with labor shortages, several issues have been pointed out from a systemic perspective.

segments.src: 一つは公的年金財政への影響だ。働く高齢者が増えることは、保険料を納める側としての側面もあり、一概に年金財政の負担増につながるわけではない。ただし、給付を受ける高齢者数そのものが増え続けていることから、現役世代とのバランスをどう維持していくかは引き続き議論の対象となっている。
segments.tr: One is the impact on public pension finances. An increase in working elderly people has aspects of contributing insurance premiums as well, so it does not necessarily lead to increased burdens on pension finances. However, since the number of elderly people receiving benefits continues to grow, how to maintain balance with the working-age population remains an ongoing subject of debate.

segments.src: もう一つは、高齢者の就労環境の整備だ。体力や健康状態に応じた柔軟な働き方、短時間勤務やテレワークの活用など、多様な選択肢を用意することが、無理のない就労継続につながるとされる。
segments.tr: Another is the development of working environments for the elderly. Providing diverse options such as flexible work arrangements suited to physical capacity and health status, part-time work, and the use of telework is said to lead to sustainable employment without overexertion.

segments.src: 今回の推計は、日本社会が「支える側」と「支えられる側」の従来の年齢区分では捉えきれない段階に入りつつあることを示している。意欲のある高齢者が働き続けられる環境を整えることは、人手不足の緩和と社会保障制度の持続性の両面で重要なテーマだ。
segments.tr: These estimates indicate that Japanese society is entering a stage that cannot be fully captured by the traditional age-based distinction between the "supporting" and "supported" populations. Creating an environment where motivated elderly people can continue working is an important issue from both the perspective of alleviating labor shortages and ensuring the sustainability of the social security system.

segments.src: 敬老の日は、長寿を祝うと同時に、高齢化が進む社会のあり方を考える機会でもある。今後も自治体や企業による就労支援、健康づくりの取り組みが、高齢者が安心して暮らし、働き続けられる社会づくりの鍵を握りそうだ。
segments.tr: Respect for the Aged Day is not only an occasion to celebrate longevity, but also an opportunity to reflect on how society should address advancing aging. Going forward, the initiatives of local governments and companies in employment support and health promotion appear to hold the key to building a society where the elderly can live with peace of mind and continue to work.
